title: Add Depot CI workflows
body:
## Summary

- Add Depot copies of the existing Checks and Work guide workflows.
- Record that this CI configuration change has no effect on the work guide's represented facts or generated HTML.

This PR follows the user's request to publish the local Depot workflow changes. No GitHub issue was identified for this change. It does not change product behavior or require an OpenSpec delta.

## Review point

- Base: `bae0b27fff80498281cf45104ca57137340a121f` (`origin/main`)
- Head: `62bd82c28fb994252fe3e8637780902f3f73efc2` (`codex/depot-ci-workflows`)
- Merge base: `bae0b27fff80498281cf45104ca57137340a121f`
- Diff: `git diff origin/main...codex/depot-ci-workflows`
- Worktree: clean at publication

## Validation

- Node 24.21.0: `npm ci`, `npm run check:workflow`, `npm run test:workflow` passed. The check found 11 valid specifications and 13 valid archived changes; all 15 workflow tests passed.
- Both Depot YAML files parsed successfully.
- Work guide generation, nine maintenance tests, and desktop/mobile/print browser checks passed. Generated HTML stayed unchanged at SHA-256 `3dc4d809ebc2b21485ee1b9405f36d1dc742430e44d7ef2b078849917a4f29b4`.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.

The guide maintenance entry is the only change under `docs/work-guide/`. Because the PR also changes `.depot/workflows/`, normal CI applies. Public guide publication and live verification are separate from this PR.

title: Add Nanoleaf general controls to the BUNNY component view
body:
The BUNNY component view rendered Nanoleaf power, brightness and scene controls as undeclared although Nanoleaf `main` 8062849 (Nanoleaf #64) now declares them on controller v1. This enables those controls in the existing Nanoleaf view under ADR 0005. Refs #153.

Power, brightness and saved-scene activation work in the Nanoleaf view without an observed session. Each control submits one guarded controller v1 command through the existing hub route with the snapshot's request ticket, configuration revision and generation. Power and brightness are available in Work, Quiet and Free; a known desired brightness is shown as an override that persists until the next explicit mode command, and no override is shown as unknown. Scene activation is disabled in Work and Quiet, while a mode change is pending or while the mode is unknown, with the reason and one explicit "Switch to Free" through the controller v1 mode command; returning to Work or Quiet uses the existing mode control. Scenes come only from the controller v1 `scenes` capability, labelled by the user-chosen names in the `nanoleaf.integration/1.0` snapshot when supplied and by ID otherwise. No command changes the mode as a side effect, nothing restores automatically, and uncertain results stay locked until the user loads current values.

**Stacked candidate.** This branch is `main` 2313df8 plus the merged branches of PR #161 (Nanoleaf #64 hub companion: scene acceptance and fixture pin, head 055aafc) and PR #160 (Pixoo #151 general controls, head 259efd8), with their work-guide conflicts reconciled in merge commit 1ef9bd2. The Nanoleaf change reuses #160's control components and needs #161's `scenes` acceptance. This PR must merge only after #161 and #160 merge; it will then be refreshed onto `main` so its diff is the Nanoleaf change alone. Until then the PR diff against `main` includes both companions. Review comparison for this change: `git diff 6dfba5e..<head>` (planning commit to head).

Scope: `apps/dashboard` source, fixture, unit and browser tests, evidence and README; the hub route test; README, architecture and development notes; OpenSpec change `gh-153-nanoleaf-general-controls` with the `unified-dashboard` delta. The hub route, controller v1 contract and Nanoleaf integration validator are unchanged here. No hook, installation, agent session, state migration or device operation. Physical acceptance on the installed wall is #155.

**Acceptance evidence at b3a5d18** (Node 24.20.0, Python 3.14.4, worktree clean at commit): `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, 10 dashboard unit tests, the main browser suite and the eleven-scenario matrix (two new #153 scenarios: Nanoleaf power and brightness in Work with the override hint, Work gating with the explicit Free switch, one guarded scene command with a preserved selection and focus across reconnect, and a controller-side scene rejection, revision conflict and uncertain result with no retry, with axe at desktop and 390px), 71 hub tests, setup, hub package, hub MCP, contract, lifecycle, agent-state and MCP suites in both languages, performance, `check:workflow` and `test:workflow`, all exit zero. Red then green: the three new client unit tests failed before the helpers existed, and the matrix failed at its first scenario before the view change; the hub route scene test passed on its first run because the shared schema already validated `scene.activate`, so it is route coverage, not a red result. Committed receipts are under `apps/dashboard/evidence`; screenshots stay outside Git.

Risk: incorrect commands can change the physical wall. Bounded by schema validation before forwarding, the controller's revision and generation guards, its typed rejection of scenes outside Free before any write, per-device serialization, typed conflicts and locked uncertain results. Transport receipts are never presented as physical results.

**UI approval scope:** the changed UI is the Nanoleaf component view under `apps/dashboard` (general controls section: power and brightness hints, Scenes group, Free switch) plus a disabled Scenes group on every other component. It is not guide UI, so explicit human approval of this exact candidate is required and is pending. Desktop and mobile screenshots of the Work and Free states were delivered to the owner outside Git.

Remaining completion work: work-guide entry and OpenSpec sync/archive commit, frozen comparison and independent Standards, Specification and accessibility reviews, all six current-head CI jobs, explicit human UI approval of the actual candidate (renewed after any UI change), merge of #161 and #160 followed by a refresh onto `main` with renewed evidence, guarded squash merge, merged-main CI readback and issue closure.

**Head e2ea41e** adds the spec sync and archive (`2026-09-22-gh-153-nanoleaf-general-controls`; `npm run check:workflow` reports 11 specifications, 0 active changes and 14 archives, and `npm run test:workflow` passes 15 tests on this head) and the work-guide refresh: backlogs refreshed, the controls guide's Nanoleaf row and the controls-music next step name PRs #160, #161 and #162, HTML SHA-256 `aef1ce56c69a81b3a7c7a047dc724da4e8c283d685038c95e4c1f798e98b7e0a`, nine maintenance tests and the desktop/mobile/print browser check passing, no generated drift after a rebuild of the committed output. The merged-history input is unchanged because this candidate records no newly merged work. This is a mixed change, so every configured CI job applies.

**Frozen comparison for review round 1:** stacked base `1ef9bd2` (merge of #161 and #160 onto `main` 2313df8), head `e2ea41e`, merge-base with `main` `2313df8`, `git diff 1ef9bd2..e2ea41e`, commits 6dfba5e, b3a5d18, e2ea41e, clean worktree, 28 files.

**Hosted checks at e2ea41e:** Work guide run 35753956127 passed. Checks run 35753956244 attempt 1: five of six jobs passed; the Dashboard job failed in the unchanged "slow device" scenario, whose direct wall snapshot read returned 429 from the hub's single per-device slot while the browser's periodic wall poll was in flight (log: `429 !== 200` at `matrix.mjs:24`). The scenario is untouched by this diff, passed in both local runs of this candidate, and carries the same signature PR #160 recorded on its head, so one evidence-supported rerun of the failed job was used for this head and signature (allowance 1 of 1). Attempt 2 passed. Readback: all six check runs on e2ea41e completed with success. The earlier b3a5d18 Work guide failure was generated-output drift before the guide commit, superseded by e2ea41e. Codex security review completed on this PR.

**Review round 1 on 1ef9bd2..e2ea41e:** Specification approved with one P3 (SPEC-1: the unknown-mode scene gating branch is covered by unit tests and inspection, not by a rendered scenario; the switch is hidden there by design). Standards approved with no findings after inspecting the helpers, the view, the fixture gating, the changed empty-sessions assertion (a strengthening: it now pins the single expected reason on Pixoo) and the privacy assertion that only `id` and `name` reach scene labels; it found no path from this diff to the slow-device 429. Both reviewers independently re-ran the unit and hub route tests (10/10 and 4/4). A separate accessibility review with a real-browser reproduction follows. The first Standards and accessibility contexts were interrupted by a session limit before returning and were replaced by fresh contexts.

Companion state: PR #161 merged as f5e71ce on 2026-09-22 with three commits after the 055aafc head this branch stacked on (scene-name validator no longer rejects newlines; guide wording; README pin), none affecting this candidate's behavior. PR #160 remains open. After #160 merges, this branch will be refreshed onto `main`, the diff re-frozen, and reviews and CI renewed on the new comparison before the guarded merge.

**Accessibility review round 1 (e2ea41e): request changes.** A11Y-1 (P1): every general-control submit disabled the focused control and dropped keyboard focus to the document without restoring it, traced with requestAnimationFrame sampling on Activate scene, Apply brightness and Switch to Free. The mechanism is shared with the Pixoo controls, but this change extends it to two new controls. All six axe scans (Work/Free, 1280px/390px, focused and hovered states) reported zero violations; accessible names, visible reasons, reading order, contrast and reduced motion checked and passing.

**Round 2 comparison:** base and merge-base with the stacked base `1ef9bd2`, head `6a37dbe`, fix diff `git diff e2ea41e..6a37dbe` (7 files), clean worktree. Fix: a `useRestoredFocus` hook in the shared draft form and one-click hook captures the focused control before its group is disabled and, once the command settles, returns focus to it or to the group's first enabled control when it is locked or unmounted. The Nanoleaf matrix scenario now activates the Free switch, a scene and the brightness form by keyboard and asserts where focus lands (red before the fix: "keyboard focus moves to the scene controls after the switch unmounts"). The scenario also waits for the refreshed snapshot before a following edit (the keyboard path exposed that the click path had only survived by timing; a stale click yields the controller's typed conflict by design), and both freeze route handlers abandon a poll still in flight at context close instead of crashing the runner, which happened in three local runs. Local evidence at 6a37dbe: typecheck, 10 unit tests, the full matrix twice, the browser suite, check:workflow and test:workflow all pass. Fix-verification reviews on the round 2 comparison (accessibility with a real-browser trace, Standards and Specification) and current-head CI follow.

**Round 2 fix verification on 6a37dbe:** accessibility approved with a real-browser trace (A11Y-1 resolved for Switch to Free, Activate scene, the locked brightness form, the uncertain-result lock, a user-redirected focus and the Pixoo Pause and Screen power controls; axe clean at both breakpoints; the committed matrix passed in that context). Standards approved; Specification approved. Recorded P3 dispositions, owner hub frontend maintenance, none blocking: SPEC-1 the unknown-mode scene gating branch is covered by unit tests and inspection, not a rendered scenario; STD-2 the focus guard cannot distinguish a deliberate blur to the page body during the busy window; A11Y-2 a fieldset-gated control still passes through the document body while its command is in flight before focus returns; STD-1 asked for the correction round's guide entry, which the refresh below records.

**Refresh onto main (round 3 comparison).** PR #161 merged as f5e71ce and PR #160 merged as d91bee7, and GitHub ran no checks on 6a37dbe while the branch conflicted with `main`. The branch was refreshed with a merge of `origin/main` (efe8933): every conflicted product file kept this branch's version because main's Pixoo content equals the 259efd8 head this branch stacked on (`git diff 259efd8 d91bee7 -- apps/dashboard …` is empty), the three hub files changed by #161 after 055aafc took main's version, and the generated guide data took main's version before regeneration. The refresh touched no #153 product file (`git diff --cached 6a37dbe -- README.md apps/dashboard apps/hub/tests docs/architecture.md docs/development.md openspec` was empty at the merge). f811083 then reconciles the guide: Hub #151 closed as completed after #160 merged, so it leaves open coverage, its candidate card and the timeline node, with a completed Pixoo reference row, a display-acceptance row for #154 and a direct reference read; backlogs and the paginated history are refreshed (hub merged PRs 71 to 72, closed issues 27 to 28, earlier entries asserted unchanged); the maintenance entry records the refresh and the correction round. Guide HTML SHA-256 `558d0386c541bc8fa9e64abcde587441552cd8024d27474fa634190c7f325ccf`; nine maintenance tests and the desktop/mobile/print browser check pass; no drift after a rebuild of the committed output.

Final comparison: base and merge-base `main` `d91bee7`, head `f811083`, `git diff d91bee7..f811083`, 33 files, clean worktree. Local evidence on the refreshed tree (efe8933, product files identical at f811083): build, typecheck, 10 dashboard unit tests, 71 hub tests, setup, hub package, hub MCP, check:workflow, test:workflow, the browser suite and the 11-scenario matrix all exit zero. Reviews of this comparison, current-head CI and human UI approval follow; the UI is unchanged since 6a37dbe, so the delivered screenshots still show the candidate.

**Second refresh (final comparison).** The #151 guide closeout PR #163 merged as bae0b27 while f811083 was open and overlapped the same guide inputs, so the branch was merged with `origin/main` again (5a0640d, guide-only conflicts: the closeout's Pixoo row, next-step text and generated data were kept, this entry's text was kept and reworded to credit #163) and the guide refreshed once more (46667b5: backlogs and paginated history refreshed, 92 primary open issues, 126 merged PRs). Product files are unchanged since 6a37dbe (`git diff 6a37dbe 46667b5 -- README.md apps/dashboard apps/hub/tests docs/architecture.md docs/development.md openspec` is empty). Guide HTML SHA-256 `7aa3c56e9d1f6a1511c43b100be8c8b298cf27eac134b360c980a3e015d59cf5`; nine maintenance tests and the desktop/mobile/print browser check pass; no drift after a rebuild of the committed output.

Final comparison: base and merge-base `main` `bae0b27`, head `46667b5`, `git diff bae0b27..46667b5`, 25 files, clean worktree. Independent Standards and Specification reviews of this comparison are in progress; the accessibility verification from round 2 stands because the UI files are byte-identical.

**Hosted checks blocked by GitHub Actions billing.** On f811083 and 46667b5 all six jobs concluded failure within seconds with zero steps, no logs, and the annotation "The job was not started because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased." This is an account-level block, not a branch failure, so no rerun allowance was used; the last hosted success for this PR is e2ea41e (six of six after one rerun) and the last successful `main` runs are d91bee7. Merge waits for the account owner to restore Actions, followed by a fresh run on the current head, in addition to the explicit human UI approval.

**Final review round on bae0b27..46667b5:** Standards approved with no findings (product diff byte-identical to the round 2 approval by hash; #161's hub files identical to main; #163's guide inputs preserved; history ordering conventions hold; a rebuild reproduces the committed HTML; no private data in the diff). Specification approved with no new findings; AC1 to AC6 hold against main, AC7 pending. Reviews of the intermediate refresh d91bee7..f811083 also approved on both axes. All reviewer contexts were fresh and read-only.

Remaining before merge, in order: (1) GitHub Actions restored by the account owner, then a fresh run on the current head with all six jobs successful; (2) explicit human UI approval of this candidate recorded here (the delivered Work and Free screenshots still show it; the UI files are unchanged since 6a37dbe); (3) guarded squash merge with `--match-head-commit`, merged-main CI readback, issue closure and a guide closeout follow-up.

title: Record 85HA keyboard and N30 mouse qualification findings
body:
The owner's packaging identifies an 8BitDo N Edition keyboard (85HA) and N30 mouse (85CA). The earlier R8 research lead does not describe this mouse. This candidate records the actual hardware, cited per-control/per-connection capabilities, Windows/Wispr/Codex interfaces, mapping ownership and a reversible operator trial.

Refs #64. This is the source-evidence candidate; #64 remains incomplete and #65 remains blocked. The keyboard's genuine held output, N30 event identities/selective suppression, installed app versions and a complete supported route are unqualified. No input observer, mapping write, microphone use, app dispatch or installation ran. Read-only Windows inventory failed because this session could not execute Windows tools.

The canonical desktop-control document and generated guide incorporate the new evidence. Guide inputs reconcile concurrent #63 closure and merged source history. Public guide publication remains separate.

Validation on the committed candidate:

- Node 24: `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow` passed; 11 specifications, 10 archives and 15 workflow tests. This documentation introduces no behavior or wire-contract delta, so no new OpenSpec capability is needed.
- `python3 docs/work-guide/work/test_maintenance.py`: all five tests passed.
- `node docs/work-guide/work/check_guide.cjs`: coverage, links, navigation, interactions and print restoration passed at six widths. Desktop/mobile/print renders were inspected. The guide covers 95 open issues, 130 linked issues, 52 roadmap nodes and nine diagrams.
- All nine Archify artifacts passed 9/9 deterministic checks; guide regeneration produced no drift. The standalone desktop-input viewer still fails its viewport check for vertical overflow, with identical dimensions and diagnostics to the previous artifact. This existing limitation is retained, not reported as a pass.

Independent Standards and Specification reviews, including Windows/input compatibility, and all six applicable hosted jobs are pending. Merge eligibility depends on their results and the missing qualification evidence; this PR has no automatic issue-closure keyword. Source work does not establish installed, application or physical acceptance.
